design_advice.implementation_summary: Add an integrated Unity EditMode validation pass that (a) samples representative Tilemap floor/wall cell world positions and representative SpriteRenderer ground-contact positions and asserts they stay geometrically consistent with the separately-owned Floor Plane collider and Wall/doorway BoxColliders without either owning the other's data, and (b) asserts EditorBuildSettings contains exactly one enabled scene (DoorPrototype.unity) and that no scene-load/SceneManager.LoadScene or cross-scene state-transfer API is referenced by gameplay/door/pursuit code, satisfying VAL-001/VAL-002 without authoring room geometry.
recommended_interfaces: A small pure-C# desync-check helper (e.g. static class comparing a Tilemap cell's world-space footprint/offset/orientation against a supplied collider bounds) usable from both the new validation tests and, optionally, an editor diagnostic menu item, so gameplay collider code never takes a compile-time dependency on Tilemap/SpriteRenderer types.

execution_recommendation.rationale: This is a bounded integration/validation pass over an already-established Unity Editor scripting pattern (LoadOrCreate*, caller-owned temp-folder test seam, EditMode desync tests already exemplified by NSC-038/NSC-039 gates). It requires moderate reasoning to design a visual-vs-collision desync check and a single-continuous-scene validation, but follows strong existing precedent in the same file/test suite and explicitly excludes room geometry/navigation, limiting architectural uncertainty. Not mechanical enough for fast; not novel/cross-system enough to require deep.
